title: Quark
summary: Interactive artificial life simulation where creatures evolve neural networks through genetic algorithms — no scripted AI, no pathfinding, no hand-tuned behaviors.
context: Quark demonstrates how complex and intelligent behavior can emerge from simple neural networks through evolution. Each creature starts with a random feed-forward network and learns only through natural selection in a living world with food, poison, climate, predation, and evolving species families.
challenges: Real-time simulation performance in the browser at higher population counts
Evolving physical traits with slider ceilings while keeping UX understandable
Visualizing neural activations live without blocking the game loop
Balancing ecosystem dynamics so emergent predation and herbivory feel natural
learnings: Fitness design shapes emergent behavior more than network size
Lab sliders as evolutionary ceilings keep experiments approachable
Decoupling PixiJS rendering from React state is essential for smooth 60fps simulation

title: PassaNota
tagline: Every receipt recorded. Every expense under control.
summary: B2B expense-control platform for Brazilian businesses — photograph fiscal receipts and let a vision LLM pipeline extract vendor, items, totals, and dates without manual entry.
context: PassaNota spans two repositories: passanota-web (Next.js frontend with BFF proxy and Supabase auth) and passanota-api (FastAPI backend with OpenCV preprocessing, vision LLM extraction, pgvector semantic search, and multi-tenant empresa isolation). Teams capture receipts on desktop or paired mobile devices; managers get spend dashboards and semantic product search.
challenges: Extracting structured data from messy thermal receipt photos without template OCR
Securing a private API on Cloud Run while forwarding Supabase user context from the web BFF
Multi-tenant isolation with empresa-scoped queries, roles, and device pairing flows
Hybrid categorization — LLM first pass plus SQL keyword and embedding refinement
learnings: Vision LLMs handle thermal receipts better than brittle OCR templates when paired with OpenCV preprocessing
A BFF with Cloud Run IAM is the cleanest pattern for a private API with Supabase JWT forwarding
pgvector HNSW enables natural-language expense search across heterogeneous product descriptions

title: Drop
tagline: Clean data. Clear insights. Immediate action.
summary: Self-serve data analysis platform — upload CSV, XLSX, or JSON spreadsheets and get instant statistical profiling, AI insights, ML recommendations, smart charts, and conversational analytics.
context: Drop spans two repositories: drop-frontend (Next.js 16 app with drag-and-drop upload, Recharts dashboard grid, and async AI polling) and drop-api (Django 5.2 REST API with pandas profiling, Google ADK/Gemini agent with tool calling, Cloud Tasks workers, and GCS file storage). Users can try anonymously or sign in via email, Google, GitHub, magic link, or QR code.
challenges: Instant results-page rendering without a second API round-trip after upload
Long-running LLM calls on Cloud Run without blocking the request thread
Dual layout UX — frictionless anonymous trial vs full sidebar for authenticated users
Build-time env injection for Next.js standalone on Cloud Run
learnings: SessionStorage upload cache eliminates results-page loading flash
Cloud Tasks with 202 + poll pattern keeps AI UX responsive under Cloud Run limits
NEXT_PUBLIC vars must be set at Docker build time for standalone Next.js deploys

title: KnowledgeHub
tagline: Personalized AI & technology intelligence, delivered weekly.
summary: Personalized technology intelligence platform that collects articles from curated sources, enriches them with AI, ranks them per user with a composite recommendation engine, and delivers tracked weekly newsletters.
context: KnowledgeHub lives in a Turborepo monorepo (newsletter-monorepo): apps/web (Next.js 16 with domain modules for auth, preferences, recommendation, newsletter, analytics, admin) and workers/collector (Python RSS/scraper pipeline with OpenAI enrichment and heuristic fallbacks). A 5-signal ranking engine blends quality, topic affinity, engagement, freshness, and diversity. Currently in local development — no public demo or GitHub URL yet.
challenges: Composite recommendation without relying solely on LLM prompt sorting
Keeping Python collector and Next.js app aligned on shared scoring primitives
Graceful degradation when Redis, OpenAI, or Resend are unavailable in local dev
Decoupling ingestion worker from web app while sharing one Prisma-managed schema
learnings: Composite scoring beats prompt-only personalization for explainability and cost control
Optional external services degrade gracefully for full local development
Shared TypeScript scoring primitives keep web ranking and worker heuristics aligned
